arxiv-2011-09834.title: Logics with Multiteam Semantics Journal: TOCL CCS: Theory of computation Logic
arxiv-2011-09834.creator: Erich Grädel, Richard Wilke
arxiv-2011-09834.description: Abstract . Team semantics is the mathematical basis of modern logics of dependence and independence. In contrast to classical Tarski semantics, a formula is evaluated not for a single assignment of values to the free variables, but on a set of such assignments, called a team.

arxiv-2207-13849.title: Arbitrarily Structured Laser Pulses
arxiv-2207-13849.creator: Jacob R. Pierce, John P. Palastro, Fei Li, Bernardo Malaca, Dillon Ramsey, Jorge Vieira, Kathleen Weichman, Warren B. Mori
arxiv-2207-13849.description: Abstract Spatiotemporal control refers to a class of optical techniques for structuring a laser pulse with coupled space-time dependent properties, including moving focal points, dynamic spot sizes, and evolving orbital angular momenta. Here we introduce the concept of arbitrarily structured laser (ASTRL) pulses which generalizes these techniques.

arxiv-2212-06683.title: UV Luminosity Density Results at z > 8 z>8 from the First JWST /NIRCam Fields: Limitations of Early Data Sets and the Need for Spectroscopy 2022 UV Luminosity Density Results at z > 8 z>8 from the First JWST /NIRCam Fields: Limitations of Early Data Sets and the Need for Spectroscopy –
arxiv-2212-06683.creator: Rychard Bouwens, Garth Illingworth, Pascal Oesch, Mauro Stefanon, Rohan Naidu, Ivana van Leeuwen, Dan Magee
arxiv-2212-06683.description: Abstract We have derived luminosity functions, and set constraints on the UV luminosity and SFR density from z ∼ 17 z\sim 17 to z ∼ 8 z\sim 8 , using the three most-studied JWST/NIRCam data sets, the SMACS0723, GLASS Parallel, and CEERS fields. We first used our own selections on two independent reductions of these datasets using the latest calibrations.

arxiv-2307-00130.title: Information Extraction in Domain and Generic Documents: Findings from Heuristic-based and Data-driven Approaches
arxiv-2307-00130.creator: Shiyu Yuan, Carlo Lipizzi
arxiv-2307-00130.description: Abstract Information extraction (IE) plays very important role in natural language processing (NLP) and is fundamental to many NLP applications that used to extract structured information from unstructured text data. Heuristic-based searching and data-driven learning are two main stream implementation approaches. However, no much attention has been paid to document genre and length influence on IE tasks.

arxiv-2311-04131.title: Towards Interpretable Sequence Continuation: Analyzing Shared Circuits in Large Language Models
arxiv-2311-04131.creator: Michael Lan, Philip Torr, Fazl Barez
arxiv-2311-04131.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Michael Lan, Philip Torr, Fazl Barez. While transformer models exhibit strong capabilities on linguistic tasks, their complex architectures make them difficult to interpret. Recent work has aimed to reverse engineer transformer models into human-readable representations called circuits that implement algorithmic functions. We extend this research by analyzing and comparing circuits for similar sequence continuation tasks, which include increasing sequences of Arabic numerals , number words , and months .

arxiv-2406-04860.title: Multi-View Stochastic Block Models
arxiv-2406-04860.creator: Vincent Cohen-Addad, Tommaso d’Orsi, Silvio Lattanzi, Rajai Nasser
arxiv-2406-04860.description: Abstract Graph clustering is a central topic in unsupervised learning with a multitude of practical applications. In recent years, multi-view graph clustering has gained a lot of attention for its applicability to real-world instances where one has access to multiple data sources.

arxiv-2406-13110.title: Denjoy-Carleman solvability of Vekua-type periodic operators
arxiv-2406-13110.creator: Alexandre Kirilov, Wagner Augusto Almeida de Moraes, Pedro Meyer Tokoro
arxiv-2406-13110.description: Abstract This paper explores the solvability and global hypoellipticity of Vekua-type differential operators on the n-dimensional torus, within the framework of Denjoy-Carleman ultradifferentiability. We provide the necessary and sufficient conditions for achieving these global properties in the case of constant-coefficient operators, along with applications to classical operators.

arxiv-2505-14526.title: RoboRAN: A Unified Robotics Framework for Reinforcement Learning-Based Autonomous Navigation
arxiv-2505-14526.creator: Matteo El-Hariry matteo.elhariry@uni.lu, Antoine Richard * antoine.richard@uni.lu, Ricard M. Castan * ricard.marsal@uni.lu, Luis F. W. Batista * luis.batista@gatech.edu, Cedric Pradalier cedric.pradalier@georgiatech-metz.fr, Matthieu Geist matthieu@earthspecies.org, Miguel Olivares-Mendez miguel.oli
arxiv-2505-14526.description: Abstract Autonomous robots must navigate and operate in diverse environments, from terrestrial and aquatic settings to aerial and space domains. While Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown promise in training policies for specific autonomous robots, existing frameworks and benchmarks are often constrained to unique platforms, limiting generalization and fair comparisons across different mobility systems.

arxiv-2510-27320.title: The quasinormal modes of the rotating quantum corrected black holes
arxiv-2510-27320.creator: Jia-Ning Chen a , b , c {}^{a\,,b\,,c}, Zong-Kuan Guo b , a , c {}^{b\,,a\,,c}, Liang-Bi Wu a , c {}^{a\,,c}
arxiv-2510-27320.description: Abstract The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a rotating quantum corrected black hole (RQCBH) are studied by employing the hyperboloidal framework for the scalar perturbation. This framework is used to cast the QNMs spectra problem into the two-dimensional eigenvalues problem, then the spectra are calculated by imposing two-dimensional pseudo-spectral method.

pmc-10574358.title: Implementation and Core Components of a Multimodal Program including Exercise and Nutrition in Prevention and Treatment of Frailty in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Narrative Review
pmc-10574358.creator: Leo Delaire, Aymeric Courtay, Joannès Humblot, Mylène Aubertin-Leheudre, France Mourey, Antoine Noël Racine, Thomas Gilbert, Zeinabou Niasse-Sy, Marc Bonnefoy
pmc-10574358.description: Increasing disability-free life expectancy is a crucial issue to optimize active ageing and to reduce the burden of evitable medical costs. One of the main challenges is to develop pragmatic and personalized prevention strategies in order to prevent frailty, counteract adverse outcomes such as falls and mobility disability, and to improve quality of life.

pmc-11457993.title: Prevalence and risk of occurrence of visible birth defects in mining areas in South Kivu: A hospital-based cross-sectional study
pmc-11457993.creator: Fabrice Gulimwentuga Cikomola, Alliance Wani Bisimwa, Arsene Daniel Nyalundja, Ernest J. Barthélemy, Bijoux Safi Matabaro, Franck Masumbuko Mukamba, Kinja Nyamugabo, Désiré Munyali Alumeti, Théophile Kabesha, Marc Miserez, Dieudonné Mushengezi Sengeyi
pmc-11457993.description: BackgroundPossible contamination related to mining activities might contribute with other risk factors in increasing the burden of birth defects (BDs) in many developing countries including the Democratic Republic of Congo. The subsequent prevalence is frequently underestimated. Implementation of focused public health interventions is hindered by the paucity of comprehensive data.

pmc-11511228.title: COVID-19 Vaccination and Vaccine Hesitancy in the Gaza Strip from a Cross-Sectional Survey in 2023: Prevalence, Risk Factors, and Associations with Health System Interventions
pmc-11511228.creator: Jennifer Majer, Jehad H Elhissi, Nabil Mousa, Jill John-Kall, Natalya Kostandova, Christian Napoli
pmc-11511228.description: Background: Preventing COVID-19 in Gaza is crucial due to the devastation of advanced health services infrastructure by war. Despite the high protection offered by COVID-19 vaccines against severe disease, a 2021 survey in Gaza found only half of the population was vaccinated, and one-third was vaccine-hesitant.

pmc-11620441.title: Building safer and more resilient cities in China: A novel approach using a dynamic nonhomogeneous Gray model for data-driven decision-making
pmc-11620441.creator: Jian Liu, Ye He, Rui Feng, Bin Lyu, Qing-Chang Lu, Qing-Chang Lu, Qing-Chang Lu
pmc-11620441.description: Urban resilience is crucial for sustainable development and resident safety in a changing environment with potential risks. Given China’s rapid urbanization, constructing resilient cities that anticipate risks, mitigate disaster impacts, and swiftly recover from crises is paramount. This study explores a key area of urban construction: building safety.

pmc-11673078.title: DT-13 Mediates Ligand-Dependent Activation of PPARγ Response Elements In Vitro
pmc-11673078.creator: Shikha Raina, Esther Samuel, Hendrik Fuchs
pmc-11673078.description: Simple SummaryInflammation poses one of the causes for progressing into the chronic stages of a disease. Therefore, it is important to find the molecules that modulate the pathways involved in inflammation. Ancient medicinal drugs involving plant substances called saponins have been recently explored as anti-inflammatory drug candidates to ameliorate inflammation.

pmc-12613431.title: Barriers and enablers of elderly care specialists towards deprescribing practices in the nursing homes: a focus group study
pmc-12613431.creator: Alireza Malek Makan, Man Chun Lee, Hein van Hein, Rob van Marum
pmc-12613431.description: IntroductionPolypharmacy increases as patients age. It is associated with a decline in quality of life and an increased risk of potentially inappropriate medications (PIMs). These are highly prevalent among long-term care residents in European countries. The potential benefits of deprescribing, as the process of withdrawing PIM’s are widespread, including improvements in both health and quality of life for patients.

pmc-13425846.creator: Nicolau Moreira Abrahão, Arthur Menino Castilho, Eduardo Tanaka Massuda, Vagner Antonio Rodrigues da Silva

pmc-13552595.title: Reported Symptoms Upon Exposure to Aeroallergen Highly Predict Allergen Sensitization Among 12‐Year‐Old Children
pmc-13552595.creator: E. Rönmark, L. Lundevall, A. Bjerg, R. Johansson, A. Winberg, L. Hedman
pmc-13552595.description: AimTo evaluate the association between reported symptoms upon exposure to airborne allergens and sensitization to the corresponding allergen.MethodIn a population‐based cohort, 1647 children aged 12 years were interviewed about symptoms from eyes, nose and lower airways upon exposure to birch, timothy, cat, dog, and horse, and were afterwards skin prick tested for the same allergens.

pmc-13570124.title: Burst swimming in sockeye salmon during their 1100 km upstream migration
pmc-13570124.creator: Kim Birnie-Gauvin, Kendra A Robinson, Evan E Byrnes, Jacey C Van Wert, Jeremy G Venditti, Steven J Cooke, Erika J Eliason, David A Patterson
pmc-13570124.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In the Fraser River (British Columbia, Canada), some sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka) populations migrate upwards of 1100 km to reach their spawning grounds and encounter challenging river conditions. Understanding how sockeye salmon partition their finite energy budget into aerobic (sustained) and anaerobic (burst) swimming could help us understand why some fish successfully make it to the spawning grounds while others do not.
